page: Amazon Web Services m8id.12xlarge is a general-purpose, Nitro-based instance designed for balanced compute, memory, and high-speed local storage throughput. The instance is powered by a 24-core, 48-thread Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor clocked at 3.9 GHz, featuring a massive 480 MB L3 cache alongside support for AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). Memory capacity is 192 GB of high-frequency DDR5 running at 7 GHz, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4 GB per virtual core. Local storage is provided by a bundled 2,850 GB NVMe SSD, supported by a 22 Gbps baseline network bandwidth profile.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong tier placement across general compute and memory-intensive metrics. The instance achieved a Geekbench multi-core score of 20,070 and a PassMark CPU score of 69,221.87, with standout results in image processing and text processing tests placing it in the top 10% tier. Memory subsystem performance shows read-only bandwidth reaching up to 3,830.37 GB/sec on cached workloads, while database operations and Redis SET throughput (86.64 million operations/sec) both landed comfortably in the top 25%. While raw stress-ng multi-core metrics sit in the middle 50%, specialized instruction workloads benefit substantially from integrated AMX and AVX-512 extensions.

Cost efficiency is maximized in operational contexts requiring fast, non-persistent working sets coupled with balanced compute. The inclusion of 2,850 GB of local NVMe storage reduces reliance on external block storage volumes for scratch data and caching layers. With balanced compute and memory density, the instance is well suited for enterprise relational databases, distributed in-memory data grids, static web serving clusters, and CPU-driven machine learning inference pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services m8id.12xlarge is a general-purpose Nitro instance equipped with 48 vCPUs (24 physical cores) from an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor running at 3.9 GHz with 480 MB of L3 cache. It provides 192 GB of DDR5 memory at 7 GHz, a 2,850 GB NVMe SSD instance store volume, and 22 Gbps baseline networking. The system excels in memory bandwidth and database benchmarks, achieving 86.64 million Redis SET operations per second and strong Geekbench multi-core marks. Hardware-accelerated matrix extensions (Intel AMX) also deliver high throughput for small-to-medium CPU-based LLM inference. With integrated high-speed local NVMe storage and balanced memory density, the m8id.12xlarge is suited for transactional databases, in-memory caching systems, CI/CD compilation, and high-throughput web serving.
